inputs.xtext_rule_text:
GuardedTargetSuccession returns SysML::TransitionUsage :
	ownedRelationship += EmptyParameterMember
	ownedRelationship += GuardExpressionMember
	'then' ownedRelationship += TransitionSuccessionMember
;

notes: re-scoped from the shared unit to sysml alone (ADR-0015)
decision: A transcription of SysML 8.2.2.17.8. The Xtext accepts the same tokens in the same order and differs only by a leading `ownedRelationship += EmptyParameterMember`, which contributes no tokens: a difference in the abstract syntax the pilot builds, not in the syntax it accepts, so the clause is followed. Unlike GuardedSuccession this production has no 'first' source and no declaration — its source is the body item that precedes it — which is what makes it the target form. The guard is mandatory, and it is the only thing separating it from the plain TargetSuccession stated two lines above it in the same clause.

evidence.note: States the production; the rule is its transcription.

Line 5 `if x == 1 then A1;` and line 6 `if x > 1 then A2;` are guarded target successions in an action body: `if x == 1` is the GuardExpressionMember, `then A1` the TransitionSuccessionMember, and the `;` is the UsageBody of the enclosing ActionTargetSuccession. Line 10 `if true then A1;` shows a literal guard.
Second opinion. Same tokens; its extra EmptyParameterMember is token-free.
